# SO3LR

> SO3LR (pronounced "Solar") is a pretrained machine-learned force field for
> (bio)molecular simulations. It combines the SO3krates neural network for
> semi-local interactions with universal pairwise force fields for short-range
> repulsion, long-range electrostatics and dispersion. Three model sizes ship
> inside the Python package. Simulations run through JAX on CPU or GPU, driven
> by a `so3lr` command-line tool, an ASE calculator, or a plain JAX potential
> function. MD runs on the "flash" engine (Pallas or CUDA GPU kernels) wherever it
> applies, and on a JAX-MD neighbour-list engine otherwise.

Key facts an agent is likely to get wrong, because they differ from other
MD codes: pressure is in bar; timesteps are in femtoseconds and should be
0.5 fs (there is no SHAKE/RATTLE); `lr_cutoff` defaults to 12 Å for periodic
systems and must be raised to 100 for molecules in vacuum; for CLI MD, a
periodic box must be at least twice `lr_cutoff` on every side; the default model
is the pinned `so3lr-tauri-m-2606`, while `so3lr-tauri-s`/`-m`/`-l` are aliases
that move between releases; the current models emit `a0_ratios`, and only the
legacy `so3lr` model emits `hirshfeld_ratios`; pre-MD relaxation frames go to a
separate `<output>_opt.xyz`. Install from a checkout with `uv sync --locked`
(Python 3.12 or 3.13). The page titled "For AI agents" collects all of these;
read it first.

## Start here

- [For AI agents](https://so3lr.github.io/advanced/llm-agents.md): SO3LR-specific traps that plausible guesses get wrong. Read before generating settings files or API calls.
- [Quick start](https://so3lr.github.io/quickstart.md): install and run a first simulation.
- [Installation](https://so3lr.github.io/installation.md): locked uv install, pip into an existing JAX (capped at jax<0.11), optional extras, troubleshooting.
- [Models](https://so3lr.github.io/models.md): so3lr-tauri-s/m/l-2606 and -2602, the legacy so3lr, supported elements, checksum verification, and why to cite the dated name.

## Running simulations

- [Command line](https://so3lr.github.io/usage/cli.md): every command and flag, exit codes, log file contents, SLURM and GPU environment variables.
- [Settings file](https://so3lr.github.io/usage/settings.md): every YAML key with defaults. Features with no command-line flag are set only here.
- [Molecular dynamics](https://so3lr.github.io/usage/md.md): ensembles, the flash and neighbour-list engines, the box-size rule, trajectory files, restarts, frozen atoms, trajectory subsetting, stability monitoring.
- [ASE calculator](https://so3lr.github.io/usage/ase.md): the Python interface, `So3lrCalculator`.
- [Dataset evaluation](https://so3lr.github.io/usage/evaluation.md): `so3lr eval`, metrics and prediction output.

## Advanced

- [Long-range electrostatics](https://so3lr.github.io/advanced/electrostatics.md): Ewald, PME and P3M; the two differently-scoped k-space arguments.
- [Enhanced sampling](https://so3lr.github.io/advanced/enhanced-sampling.md): PySAGES, collective variables, the cylindrical restraint, free-energy extraction.
- [Observables](https://so3lr.github.io/advanced/observables.md): energy components, partial charges, embeddings, and which names each interface accepts.
- [Gradients and Hessians](https://so3lr.github.io/advanced/derivatives.md): second derivatives and observable Jacobians.
- [Binding energies](https://so3lr.github.io/advanced/binding-energies.md): dimer interaction energies.
- [Custom integrations](https://so3lr.github.io/advanced/integrations.md): the bare JAX potential and the JAX-MD binding, for embedding SO3LR elsewhere.

## Training

- [Fine-tuning](https://so3lr.github.io/training/finetuning.md): strategies, and why forces-only data needs `freeze_long_range`.
- [Training from scratch](https://so3lr.github.io/training/from-scratch.md): config, multiple datasets, robust loss, opt-in W&B logging.

## Reference

- [Python API](https://so3lr.github.io/reference/api.md): signatures of the public surface and the model registry.
- [Datasets](https://so3lr.github.io/reference/datasets.md): the Zenodo archive and label conventions.
- [Changelog](https://so3lr.github.io/reference/changelog.md): model releases and package changes, including changes that alter results.
- [FAQ](https://so3lr.github.io/reference/faq.md): cutoffs, precision, engines, drift, common errors.

## Optional

- [Examples](https://so3lr.github.io/examples.md): runnable notebooks, including a zero-install Colab.
- [Contributing](https://so3lr.github.io/contributing.md): repository layout, the lockfile, tests and CI, adding a model release or a settings key, licence.
- [How to cite](https://so3lr.github.io/cite.md): BibTeX for the SO3LR Tauri preprint and the JACS and SO3krates papers, and how to name the software version and dated model.
- [llms-full.txt](https://so3lr.github.io/llms-full.txt): every page concatenated into one file.
